title: Not

brief.story: A night light should be on when the light sensor says it's NOT bright. SA stands in for the sensor: on means bright. Q1 is the transistor switch from 0–10, with its base resistor fitted. The output still needs its pull-up resistor, from + to Q1's collector.
brief.goal: Add the pull-up resistor so LED1 is lit when SA is off and dark when SA is on: a NOT gate (an inverter).

hints: With Q1 off, the pull-up resistor lifts the output (column 12) to + and current flows through it into LED1. With Q1 on, Q1 pulls the output down to about 0.2 V and LED1 goes dark.
The pull-up goes from the + rail to column 12, Q1's collector.
Try 1 kΩ: (9 V − 2 V) ÷ 1 kΩ = 7 mA into the LED when Q1 is off. 100 Ω would burn it; 10 kΩ is too dim.

spec.label: LED1 = NOT SA
spec.explain: The output is pulled up to + through the resistor, and Q1 pulls it down when SA turns it on.

debrief: One transistor and a pull-up resistor make NOT: the output is high unless the transistor pulls it low. Every logic chip is built from inverters like this, only with MOSFETs and billions of them.
